newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to temporarily add reserves to the banking system on Wednesday via overnight system repurchase agreements, analysts said.

"We expect overnight system RPs," said Bill Griggs, a managing director at Griggs and Santow. "There is quite a bit of firmness in the federal funds and the Fed has RPs maturing tomorrow. They'll do overnight systems today and come back to do more tomorrow."
Ahead of the 1130 EDT/1530 GMT usual intervention time, fed funds traded at 5-7/16, above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target.
The funds rate is under pressure, due in part to a rise in currency in circulation ahead of the three-day U.S. Labor Day weekend.
Seven-day and three-day fixed system repo operations are expiring at the start of business on Thursday, the beginning of a new reserve maintenance period.
